Accept it.

In theory, but the introvert/extrovert is where you get your energy from. So if get tired from too much people and need to recharge, you're likely an introvert. This doesn't mean that you don't enjoy people or aren't social. An extrovert on the other hand gets energy from being around people. The usual distinction is if you could stay at home on your own for a day and not care, you're probably introvert, but if that would drive you crazy and you would need to be around people before the day is up, extrovert.

To change the way you respond would be similar to reconditioning. So changing the negative to positive. At most I'd say someone can go to around a neutral, being neither introvert or extrovert, without a major personality change.

Not really. That's like saying you where born strait but want you switch your brain to gay, because the dating would be easier.

I enjoy being an introvert, but I know society is a social thing. So I make it a point to have social activities I can get life experience from. I just choose things that don't take such a mental toll. Like group activities ( board games, pen and paper RPG's, Vampire the Masquerade(its a LARP you can do anywhere), paintball, mountain climbing/biking, etc, etc)

You can't "fix" your introversion, but you can manage it, assuming its to much of a toll.

It's a lot easier for introverts to 'spoof' the behaviour of an extrovert than vice versa. It's exhausting and usually short term but it's entirely possible. What kinds of behaviour are you seeking to replicate?
